parameters.content:
## Log Shopify, Etsy and Square orders to a Google Sheet and confirm by email

**Who's it for**
Small makers and studios taking orders from more than one storefront, who still retype each one into a spreadsheet and write the confirmation email by hand.

**How it works**
A store webhook posts an order. `read the order` works out whether the payload is Shopify, Etsy or Square and pulls the same facts out of each shape; a Square order whose deposit has not landed is held. The order is matched against the board so a retried webhook is never written twice, every line item is checked against the product rules, and the ship window is worked out in working days from the longest lead time. The row is written to the sheet **before** the confirmation email goes out, then stamped confirmed.

**How to set up**
1. Open `config`, set `BOARD_SHEET_ID` and `BOARD_TAB`, then set `BOARD_READY = true`.
2. Attach Google Sheets and Gmail credentials to the four `[cred]` nodes.
3. Point the store webhook at this workflow's production URL.
4. Leave `TEST_RUN = true` for the first run, read the preview, then set it to `false`.

**Requirements**
A Google Sheets credential, a Gmail credential, and an `Orders` tab with the headings listed in `config`. A blank setting skips a step rather than failing the run.

**How to customize**
`PRODUCT_RULES` holds the lead time and wall-anchor rule per sku; the two buffers set how wide the promised window is. Email wording lives in `compose the confirmation`.

### 1. Take the order in and read it

`An order arrives` receives the POST from Shopify, Etsy or Square. `config` holds every setting in one place - sheet id, product rules, email wording and the test switch - and is the only node you edit.

`read the order` detects the store from the shape of the payload and turns it into one common order object. `a usable order?` checks there is a customer email, an order number and at least one line item, and holds a Square order until its deposit is received.

### 2. Match it against the board

`board connected?` reads `BOARD_READY`. With a sheet configured, `[cred] Sheets - read the board` pulls the whole `Orders` tab; without one, `use the demo board` emits the same shape from built-in demo rows, so the workflow can be run end to end before a single credential exists.

`seen this order before?` folds those rows into one answer and `already logged?` drops a redelivered webhook, so the same store order is never written to the board twice.

### 3. Plan the build, promise an honest window

`plan the build` looks up every line item in `PRODUCT_RULES`, takes the longest lead time in the order and adds the two buffers in working days only, so no promise lands on a weekend.

`every product known?` holds any order containing a sku the rules do not cover - a missing rule is a gap, never a guess. `compose the confirmation` then writes the email, quoting only numbers the plan produced.

### 4. Write the row first, then send

`board ready to write?` and `row for the board` hand a clean headings-only row to `[cred] Sheets - log the order (row first)`, so the order is on the board before anything is emailed.

`sending the confirmation?` is the safety gate: `[cred] Gmail - send the confirmation` runs only in test or live mode. `row: mark confirmed` and `[cred] Sheets - mark confirmed` stamp the timestamp and the `Confirmed` stage afterwards, so the board never claims an email that did not go.

### 5. Every path ends with an answer to the store

Each `STOP:` node closes one path and keeps the reason on the item, so the execution list says exactly why: not a usable order, a duplicate delivery, a sku with no product rule, demo mode (nothing written or sent) or preview mode (row written, email withheld). Open a STOP node's output to read the row and the email that would have been produced.

`Reply to the store` answers the webhook on every path, so the storefront stops retrying whichever way the order went.
